# check-opencloud-security: extended agent guide

This is an independent OpenCloud security scanner. It measures what a public,
unauthenticated visitor can observe: release support, known advisories, TLS,
HTTP security headers, hardening signals, and exposed services. It does not
authenticate, test accounts or stored data, assess the host or network, or
replace a penetration test.

The scanner grades the measured result from 0 to 5 (A+ to F). A scan UUID is a
bearer capability: do not disclose it, guess it, or put it in an issue, log,
or public document. Results expire after the service retention period; an
unknown, expired, malformed, or erased UUID always returns `404`.

## Authoritative contracts

- [Discovery document](/.well-known/ai.json): service-specific entry point.
- [OpenAPI 3.1](/openapi.json): endpoint and schema authority.
- [Arazzo 1.0.1](/arazzo.json): asynchronous API workflow authority.
- [MCP](/mcp): task interface when enabled by the operator, and the knowledge
  base described below.
- [API guide](/api), [agent guide](/ai), and [privacy policy](/privacy): human
  explanations of the same public interface.

The discovery document is an application convention, not a registered
standard. Its URLs, the OpenAPI document, and the Arazzo document are the
authoritative machine contracts. This file, `/llms.txt` and `/agents.txt` are
all explanatory and must not override them; `/agents.txt` is itself an
informal convention, published alongside `/robots.txt` for a fetcher that
looks for one of those two filenames before anything else, and reuses
`/robots.txt`'s own allow/disallow list so the two can never disagree about
what is off limits.

## Knowledge base

Two of the MCP endpoint's five resources are reference material rather than a
task or a contract, so an agent can use them without ever submitting a scan:

- `catalogue` (`spec://check-opencloud-security/catalogue.json`): every
  hardening flag and extra check the scanner runs, grouped by category, with
  the OpenCloud setting behind it where one exists, how to fix it, and a link
  to the official documentation.
- `advisories` (`spec://check-opencloud-security/advisories.json`): the whole
  advisory database a scan is rated against - every known advisory's
  severity, affected version ranges and fixed release, not only the ones
  that matched one instance's reported version.

Both resources are generated by calling the same functions the
[`/catalogue`](/catalogue) page renders from, so an agent reading the
resource and a person reading the page can never be told something different
about the same check id. Read `catalogue` to explain a finding by its id, or
`advisories` to see what the scanner would flag, before or instead of running
a scan.

## Safe use

Only scan a public OpenCloud instance the caller is responsible for or has
permission to test. The service rejects private, loopback, link-local, and
cloud metadata addresses. Requests may choose `target_url`,
`ignore_hardenings`, `release_track`, and `output_format`; timeout,
concurrency, TLS verification, and worker settings are server-side only.

Submit one target with `POST /api/scans`, then poll
`GET /api/scans/{uuid}`. `202` means queued; `200` can still mean queued or
running; `404` is final; `429` supplies `Retry-After`; and an export can
return `409` until the scan has completed. Use the Arazzo workflow rather than
inventing a polling or retry policy.

The task-level MCP tools are `scan_instance`, `scan_instances`,
`get_scan_result`, `plan_remediation`, `export_scan`, and
`erase_instance_data`. The last is destructive and requires the same
operator authorisation as the HTTP erasure endpoint. MCP and browser WebMCP
execute the public API; they do not bypass SSRF protection, rate limits,
queueing, or result isolation.

## Release and advisory evidence

The bundled release lifecycle and advisory database are checked-in evidence
used by the offline scanner. CI refreshes both through reviewable pull
requests. The web worker may refresh its in-memory copies, but accepts only
conservative updates: schedules cannot lose known support facts, and
advisories cannot lose known affected ranges. A new release is not assumed
compatible; the integration workflow tests the scanner against an OpenCloud
container and the refresh PR runs the relevant regression tests before review.

## Privacy and limits

This service has no account or API key. It queues work rather than returning
`503` for a valid submission, and rate limits are a prompt to run the
open-source scanner locally. The service does not publish a scan listing.
Search engines are instructed not to index scan pages, API results, or
exports. See [/privacy](/privacy) for the retention and logging model.
